Title: Cyrena.Desk - Scheduled Agent Architecture
Content:
# Cyrena.Desk - Scheduled Agent Architecture

## Purpose
Cyrena.Desk is a scheduled-agent execution platform. A `ScheduledAgent` row binds a
`ChatConfiguration` to a `Schedule` and an `Instruction`. The scheduler loads a kernel
for each due agent, runs the instruction through `IIterationService`, and computes
the next fire time when the agent completes.

## Projects
- `Cyrena.Desk.Core` — contracts + models only. Pure data and pure logic
  (e.g. `Schedule.Next(...)`). No DI, no I/O, no hosts.
- `Cyrena.Desk.Extension` — wiring + implementations. The host service lives here.
  The `DeskExtension.BuildExtension` method is the single place where Desk
  services are registered.

## Architectural rules
- Scheduling decisions (next-execution calculation, fail-pause, etc.) live in the
  host service, not in `AgentInstance`. `AgentInstance` only signals
  "iteration ended" and exposes a `MarkComplete()` hook for a future completion
  kernel function to call.
- `IIterationService.Iterate()` is fire-and-forget from the scheduler's
  perspective — it runs in a queue we cannot control. Use `IIterationService.Cancel`
  if a scheduled agent must be aborted.
- `Schedule.Next(from)` returns `null` for `ScheduleInterval.None`. The host
  service treats this as "delete the agent and log".
- `AgentInstance.Initialize()` is idempotent and thread-safe via
  `Interlocked.CompareExchange`.
- Completion validation (the "on complete" kernel function) is a future piece of
  work. Until it is wired up, an agent's `Complete` flag will only be set if some
  external code calls `AgentInstance.MarkComplete()`.
- **Settings retrieval rule (HARD RULE)**: `AgentOptions` and any other app-level
  option type MUST be retrieved via `ISettingService`, NEVER via
  `Microsoft.Extensions.Options.IOptions<T>` / `IOptionsSnapshot<T>` /
  `IOptionsMonitor<T>`. Reason: users must be able to change these values at
  runtime through the settings UI. `IOptions<T>` binds at startup and never
  updates; it is the wrong abstraction for anything user-tunable. This is a
  project-wide rule, not Desk-specific.
- **Notification type registration**: `NotificationOptions.AddNotificationType`
  throws `InvalidOperationException` on duplicate `typeId`. This is a
  configuration bug, not a recoverable condition.
- **Notification lifecycle (terminal = delete)**: `INotificationService.DismissAsync`
  deletes the row from the store and fires `OnNotificationDismissed`. There is
  no "soft dismiss" — dismissing a notification removes it. `DeleteAsync` is the
  silent variant (no event). The `OnNotificationDismissed` contract comment says
  it also covers "interaction complete OR expiration" but only the explicit
  `DismissAsync` path is currently implemented. Auto-dismiss on `ExpiresAt` is a
  future sweep.
- **Notification subscription hygiene**: Subscribers must `Dispose` the
  `IDisposable` returned by `OnNotificationReceived` / `OnNotificationDismissed`.
  In Blazor components, dispose in the component's `IDisposable.Dispose`.
  Forgetting this leaks subscriptions across navigations.

## Cross-project dependency rules
- `Cyrena.Desk.Extension` references `Cyrena.Desk.Core`.
- Neither project references the other extension projects; Desk is consumed by
  the host at runtime via the extension manifest.

## Non-goals
- The completion-validation kernel function is out of scope for the current
  scheduler pass. TODO is marked on `AgentInstance.OnIterationEnd`.
- `AgentOptions.MaxAgentIterations` enforcement (kill-after-N-iterations) is not
  yet wired in the scheduler; the type exists in `Cyrena.Desk.Core/Options` and
  will be read via `ISettingService` when the time comes.
- Kill-after-N-failures is not yet implemented. TODO is in
  `SchedulerHostedService.DispatchDueAgentsAsync`.
- Razor components for agent management are not implemented yet. The
  `Components/` folder has only `_Imports.razor` and an empty
  `DefaultNotification.razor` placeholder.
- Auto-dismiss sweep for `Notification.ExpiresAt` is not implemented.

## API Reference
- `cyrena-desk-notification-service` — `INotificationService` and
  `NotificationService` (the entire consumer-facing notification surface).
